revisionNote: Third R62 draft, rebuilt from live U1.123. It supersedes db805b9 and 6aab98c, neither of which was published. The user found their pathing forced and unnatural, and out of the site's style. Causes found: new questions of 13 to 16 words (site median 9), yes/no gates inserted into other families' chains, and the site's multi-answer questions taken apart. This draft adds no new question wording. Two new nodes repeat the site's own question 'Should national interests come before all other commitments?'. One question is reworded and shortened from 13 to 10 words, and one question is removed because after the moves it would separate nothing. Existing branches are moved whole.

changes.change: Renamed National syndicalism (JONS). The old name is not kept as an alias, because aliases are displayed as 'Also known as'.

changes.change: The existing branch (q_natSynd with q_fumivFascfu and q_nazbol) moves whole from the 'No' side of q_markets to the 'Yes' side. It now follows q_authMarkSoc Yes through a new node, q_natMarket, which repeats the site's question 'Should national interests come before all other commitments?'. Answering No leads to the existing price question (q_guilds), so market, Langean and guild socialism are reached as before with one added question. Their anti-property placement is unchanged.
changes.rationale: The old route required these four to deny that market exchange should remain a lasting institution. None of their programmes abolishes exchange. Their placement on the anti-property side is defensible: the Ba'ath constitution makes socialism necessary and puts large industry under national ownership; Sun Yat-sen equated the principle of livelihood with socialism; and the Carta del Carnaro makes labour the only legitimate title to property in means of production and exchange.
sources: Carta del Carnaro (1920), De Ambris text, art. 2 ('una democrazia diretta che ha per base il lavoro produttivo') and art. 6 (property as a social function; labour as 'il solo titolo legittimo di proprietà su qualsiasi mezzo di produzione e di scambio'); corporations' members earn 'salario, stipendio, profitto d'azienda, o lucro professionale'. PDFs at silvanapoli.it and twiki.di.uniroma1.it, read 2026-11-27

changes.change: Moves from the centralized-state branch to the branch for No to 'Should revolutionary socialism be built through centralized state authority?'. After the existing unions question (q_unions No), a new node, q_natSocLib, repeats 'Should national interests come before all other commitments?': Yes leads to Third International Theory, No to Libertarian socialism. q_classStruggleTool ('Should class struggle serve national purification and renewal?') is removed, because after the move only one answer would remain; q_natSocAuth Yes now leads straight to q_nationalCouncils, so the National Bolshevik results lose one question and nothing else. q_nazbol loses 'Direct Democracy' because Third International Theory no longer passes through it; Ba'athism and Tridemism keep 'Vanguard' and 'Parliament'.
changes.rationale: Third International Theory stays on the 'No' side of q_markets: the Green Book's final stage has no profit or money. Its adherents could not honestly assent to centralized state authority: the Green Book rejects party rule and representation and gives authority to the popular congresses. Its distinctive claim against libertarian socialism is national: the 'national factor' drives history and the national state is the natural political form.
sources: The Green Book, Part One (marxists.org ch01, read 2026-11-27): 'The party is a contemporary form of dictatorship.'; 'There can be no representation in lieu of the people and representation is fraud.'; 'Popular Conferences are the only means to achieve popular democracy.'
The Green Book, Part Two (marxists.org ch02, read 2026-11-27): 'The final step is for the new socialist society to reach a stage in which profit and money disappear.'

The Green Book, Part Three (marxists.org ch03, read 2026-11-27): 'The social factor, the national factor, is the dynamic force of human history.'; 'The national state is the only political form which is consistent with the natural social structure.'
Library of Congress Country Study, Libya, 'The Green Book' (countrystudies.us): secondary, corroborates Part Two

changes.node: q_demCent, Spartacism, Council Communism (Organizational Dualism), Italian Left-Communism (Battaglia)
changes.change: q_demCent shortened from 'Should a centralized vanguard party provide political leadership in the proletarian revolution?' to 'Should a centralized vanguard party direct the proletarian revolution?'. Spartacism moves to the No side, next to council communism: the existing question q_parliamentaryAgitation now follows q_partyElites Yes, with Yes leading to Spartacism and No to Council Communism (Organizational Dualism). Battaglia now ends at q_organic No.
changes.rationale: Under the old wording a Luxemburgist could answer Yes, which is why Spartacism sat in the vanguard branch. Luxemburg accepted a centralizing tendency in Social Democracy but rejected Lenin's 'ultra-centralism' (1904). The Spartacus League's programme refuses to take power over or through the working masses. The parliament question is the real historical line between the two council-side currents: at the KPD founding congress Luxemburg, Liebknecht and Levi argued for contesting the National Assembly elections and lost 62 to 23, and the KAPD later rejected parliamentarism.
sources: Luxemburg, 'Was will der Spartakusbund?', Die Rote Fahne, 14 Dec 1918 (marxists.org German, read 2026-11-27): 'Der Spartakusbund ist keine Partei, die über die Arbeitermasse oder durch die Arbeitermasse zur Herrschaft gelangen will.'
